models.name: Model A: Lumen Flow CFD
models.what_it_computes: Steady, incompressible Navier–Stokes solution inside the catheter lumen to predict pressure drop, wall shear stress, and flow partitioning with and without a guidewire present.

models.name: Model B: External Flow CFD with Imposed Advancement
models.what_it_computes: Transient, pulsatile external flow around the catheter within an idealized vessel curve with prescribed catheter advancement; computes surface shear/pressure distributions, net lateral tip force, and unsteady drag.

mechanisms.name: M1: Lumen pressure drop at clinical infusion rates
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Determines flow resistance, informing maximum deliverable flow rate and label claims for infusion and contrast delivery.

mechanisms.name: M2: Outer-surface shear and drag during advancement
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Contributes to the force required to track the catheter through tortuous vessels and affects controllability during navigation.

mechanisms.name: M3: Lateral tip force from asymmetric outlet geometry
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Side holes and bevels can induce cross-stream forces that bias steering and affect trackability around bends.

mechanisms.name: M4: Flow-induced distal shaft oscillations
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Unsteady hydrodynamic loading can promote tip oscillation that degrades control and may elevate local vessel wall stresses.

deviation.detail: All factor scores are reported on a 0–7 Credibility Index, assigned separately for each (model × mechanism) pair.

expected_decision.outcome_source: The integrated judgment supports use of Model A for claims and design choices tied to lumen hydraulics within the studied ranges, and use of Model B for comparative design screening of external drag and lateral biasing in moderate tortuosity, with additional evidence required for oscillation amplitudes and for severe anatomical scenarios.

expected_context_of_use: The context of use (COU) for the internal-flow model is to support design selection and labeling for maximum deliverable flow rate through the catheter lumen when driven by a standard syringe or pump, with and without a guidewire, for contrast bolus delivery and medication infusion. For the external-flow model, the COU is to support design selection and optimization for navigation in moderately tortuous environments, covering curved vessel segments with bend angles of 30°, 60°, and 90° and radii 20–40 mm, for coronary-sized vessels (2.5–4.0 mm diameter).

spans: Dimensional metrology was conducted on 20 catheters sampled from three production lots using a combination of optical microscopy for distal features (side holes, bevel angle) and pin gages/micro-CT for lumen diameter and wall thickness.
findings.span: Dimensional metrology was conducted on 20 catheters sampled from three production lots using a combination of optical microscopy for distal features (side holes, bevel angle) and pin gages/micro-CT for lumen diameter and wall thickness.

spans: The observed order of accuracy for ∆p at 10 mL/s was 1.98, with a grid-convergence index (GCI) of 1.2% between the fine and medium meshes using a 95% confidence factor.
findings.span: The observed order of accuracy for ∆p at 10 mL/s was 1.98, with a grid-convergence index (GCI) of 1.2% between the fine and medium meshes using a 95% confidence factor.

spans: Model A predictions of ∆p(Q) matched the bench data within a mean absolute error of 4.3% across the 1–15 mL/s range for bare lumen, 4.9% with a 0.014 in guidewire, and 6.2% with a 0.018 in guidewire.
Model A attained high credibility for M1 (scores 5–7 across factors) with mean absolute error of 4.3% versus measured pressure drop across 1–15 mL/s and strong mesh convergence.

For example, steady-state pressure drop per unit length at specified volumetric flow is the same quantity read out during syringe-driven flow bench testing.

spans: For the internal-flow model and its companion experiments, boundary conditions were volumetric-flow inlets set by sy-ringe pumps and outlets held at atmospheric pressure.
Flow rates covered 0.1–15 mL/s.
The minor losses associated with connectors and luer fittings were measured and subtracted from bench data to isolate catheter-only ∆p.
findings.span: For the internal-flow model and its companion experiments, boundary conditions were volumetric-flow inlets set by sy-ringe pumps and outlets held at atmospheric pressure.

spans: In Model B, halving ∆t from 0.2 ms to 0.1 ms and increasing the mesh from 7.9 million to 15.8 million cells reduced the root-mean-square unsteady drag over a cycle by 2.1% and the peak lateral force by 2.6%.
The power spectral density of the unsteady drag changed negligibly with further refinements: the integrated area over 0–20 Hz varied by 2.7% when halving ∆t from 0.2 ms to 0.1 ms.

spans: For Model B, the RMS unsteady drag error across all vessel diameters and bend severities was 7.0% (N = 27 condition combinations), with dominant harmonic phase errors under 6°.
